# Live audit regression structures

These synthetic fixtures retain the field types and ordering relevant to the
2026-10-13 audit at commit 3e99ec1. IDs, model names, prompts, and error messages
have been replaced. No credentials, signatures, or provider instructions are
included. They prove structural behavior, not vendor signature acceptance.

Source evidence in run `2026-10-13T04-31-20.856Z-b6e1d87f`:

| Fixture | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| safety_buffering | 0426-call-record.json |
| unknown_failure | 0445-call-record.json |
| upstream_error | 0409-call-record.json |
| rate_limit / invalid_usage_tail | 0387-call-record.json |
| tool_choice_request / tool_choice_failure | 0405-call-record.json |
| output_text | 0446-call-record.json |
| heartbeat | 0432-call-record.json |
| changed_chat_identity | 0404-call-record.json |
| incomplete_start | protocol/evidence/request-0022.json |
| direct_http_failure | protocol/evidence/request-0010.json |
| code_check_timeout | code/backend-tests and 0914-backend-tests.log |

The `***.failed` event name is present in the original evidence; it is not a
redaction made by these fixtures. Unknown failed events and inconsistent IDs
must remain failures. Tests add complete valid streams to the first-frame
fixtures, since the captured gateway calls stopped before receiving the rest.

The concurrency-one paired replay on 2026-10-13 subsequently observed
`safety_buffering:false` on `response.in_progress`,
`response.output_text.delta`, and `response.completed` as well as the initial
event. Complete-stream tests now cover these four explicit locations. Other
locations and cross-protocol `true` remain unsupported. That replay also
captured a code-only `upstream_error` inside an invalid `***.failed` event;
its primary upstream category and secondary event-contract error are separate.
